text: Use inverse user-impression-count weights in binary cross-entropy so highly active users do not dominate training updates.
rationale: Official nDCG@5 is macro-averaged across users, whereas unweighted row loss gives more influence to users with many training impressions. User-frequency segments show differentiated behavior, so a user-balanced loss is a ranking-aligned training ablation.
exact_ablation: Replace only unweighted binary cross-entropy in experiment 1 with binary cross-entropy weighted by the reciprocal of each user's count of training impressions, normalized to mean weight one; retain all model, feature, optimizer, seed, and schedule settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0003 to +0.0015 because user balancing may trade dominant-user fit for macro ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0000 to +0.0020 because the training weighting better matches macro per-user top-five evaluation.
